description: Make epic close non-destructive (retain links) and refine the issue↔epic uniqueness invariant to 'at most one non-terminal epic per issue', with primaryEpic projection reflecting non-terminal membership.

tasks.title: Non-destructive close and status-aware membership uniqueness
tasks.description: Remove the close→unlink side-effect from EpicGrain.ApplyPendingEvents (delete the EpicClosed branch and RemoveAllLinkedIssues helper) so closing an epic retains all EpicIssueRow links. Relax the unique DB index IX_EpicIssues_ProjectId_IssueId to non-unique via an EF Core migration so a terminal-epic membership and a new non-terminal membership can coexist. Replace the single-row duplicate check in LinkIssueAsync with a set-based, status-aware query that rejects DUPLICATE_EPIC_MEMBERSHIP only when an existing membership belongs to a different non-terminal epic; terminal-epic memberships do not block re-homing. UnlinkIssueAsync stays unchanged. Cover all changes with Fake-based specs.
acceptanceCriteria: Closing an epic transitions it to `closed` and all N linked-issue memberships remain present (assert member list + progress preserved post-close).
An issue held only by terminal (done/closed) epic(s) can be linked to a non-terminal (idle/running/paused) epic without DUPLICATE_EPIC_MEMBERSHIP; the terminal membership row remains intact.
Linking an issue that already belongs to a non-terminal epic into a second non-terminal epic is still rejected with DUPLICATE_EPIC_MEMBERSHIP and no second non-terminal membership is created.
The duplicate check is idempotent: linking an issue to an epic it already belongs to (any status) does not error and does not create a duplicate row.
Explicit unlink of a single membership still removes exactly one link and leaves other memberships (including terminal-epic ones) intact.
Epic progress, member list, and detail reads for a newly-closed epic show the preserved member set (non-empty) instead of an empty set.
EF Core migration drops the unique constraint on IX_EpicIssues_ProjectId_IssueId (index kept as non-unique) and MohistDbContextModelSnapshot is updated; `npm test` passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors.
tasks.output: Modified EpicGrain.cs (removed close side-effect + status-aware LinkIssueAsync), new EF Core migration + updated ModelSnapshot, updated/new specs in EpicLifecycleSpecs.cs and epic membership specs; `npm test` green.
tasks.notes: Rewrite Close_SetsStatusToClosedAndRemovesEpicIssueLinks (EpicLifecycleSpecs.cs) → Close_SetsStatusToClosedAndRetainsEpicIssueLinks. Fix the Assert.Empty(detail.LinkedIssues) assertion in Close_DoesNotChangeIssueStatus… → assert the linked issue is still present. Reuse EpicProgress.IsTerminal(string) for the terminal-status test in the duplicate check to avoid a second definition of 'terminal'. The EpicClosed domain event stays emitted (audit) but now has no subscriber.

tasks.title: primaryEpic projection reflects non-terminal membership
tasks.description: Update the IssueQuerier primaryEpic projection (IssueQuerier.cs around line 1258-1281) so issue.PrimaryEpic is assigned only from a membership whose owning epic is non-terminal (idle/running/paused). An issue whose epic memberships are all terminal (done/closed) projects null primaryEpic. When an issue is re-homed from a terminal epic to a new non-terminal epic, the projection follows the new non-terminal epic. Reuse EpicProgress.IsTerminal(string) for the status test.
acceptanceCriteria: An issue that is a member of exactly one non-terminal epic projects that epic as its primaryEpic.
An issue whose epic memberships are all terminal (done/closed) projects null primaryEpic.
After re-homing an issue from a terminal epic to a new non-terminal epic, primaryEpic references the new non-terminal epic and does not reference the terminal epic.
Fake-based specs cover the three primaryEpic scenarios (non-terminal membership, terminal-only → null, re-homing follow); `npm test` passes.
tasks.output: Modified IssueQuerier.cs (primaryEpic projection filters terminal-epic memberships); new/updated specs in IssueQuerier specs; `npm test` green.
tasks.notes: Because T-001 guarantees at most one non-terminal membership per issue, the existing 'last write wins' loop naturally resolves to that single non-terminal epic once terminal memberships are filtered out — no explicit ordering needed. Verify no other read path assumed primaryEpic was always non-null for issues with epic memberships.
